name: Jigawa
summary_text: Jigawa is within the twelve-state Sharia criminal-law bloc adopted between 1999 and 2002. Sharia courts have criminal jurisdiction over Muslims, and the penal code extends criminalisation to same-sex acts between women, which the federal SSMPA does not cover independently. No trans-specific incident or Hisbah documentation exists for Jigawa in this dossier. The legal architecture is the finding; under-reporting is structural (TIERs and UK CPIN both flag data limitations). Score 0.024 below the national 0.08, identical to the other generic-Sharia states (Borno, Gombe, Kaduna, Katsina, Kebbi, Niger). The deviation rests on the enacted parallel system rather than documented enforcement. Above Yobe (0.04) and Zamfara (0.05), where Hisbah presence is specifically named.

sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch report (2004) on the extension of Sharia to criminal law in Nigeria: Zamfara's governor was first, introducing the Sharia Establishment Law on 27 October 1999 (in force 27 January 2000), and by 2002 twelve northern states had adopted some form of Sharia into their criminal legislation - to date the only states where Sharia courts have jurisdiction to try criminal cases.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (HTTP 403); the underlying USCIRF study of Sharia criminal-law implementation covers Kano, Sokoto and Zamfara using 173 cases from 2017, confirming operational Sharia-court function in Zamfara.
